cases.question: Our class is building a poster about water and heat in the Mekong Delta. Which records would be worth a look?

expected.rationale: Broad goal at a reviewed region; water and heat quantities are relevant, and each suggestion must cite its own variable's section.

cases.question: I volunteer at a ski club in the Alps. What records would help me understand how the mountain winters have been changing?

expected.rationale: Broad goal about winters at a reviewed region; snow and cold quantities are relevant. A DJF season or the full year are both reasonable readings; the premise that winters have changed must not be stated as fact.

cases.question: We run a small solar-panel cooperative in Johannesburg. Which records are relevant to how our conditions have changed?

expected.rationale: Broad goal about solar conditions; sunlight, cloud, haze and heat are relevant. Sunlight and cloud start in 1984, which record_start covers.

cases.question: A farmer group on the Great Plains asked me which NASA records would describe their growing-season conditions over the years. What would you point them to?

expected.rationale: Broad agricultural goal at a reviewed region; rainfall, soil wetness and temperature are relevant. Growing season names no catalogue season, so any season is accepted.

cases.question: I want the depth of lying snow in Sapporo. Is that something the app has?

expected.rationale: Snow depth is in the catalogue; the suggestion must cite the snow-depth note or a MERRA-2 FAQ section on SNODP.

cases.question: Manila: what would describe all the moisture held in the air above the city, not just near the ground?

expected.rationale: The whole-column quantity is water vapour in the air column, not two-metre humidity.

expected.rationale: Surface air pressure; Quito is high, which the catalogue note and POWER's surface-pressure sections address.

cases.question: Lusaka farmers talk about the topsoil drying out quickly. What could show how wet the top few centimetres of soil are?

expected.rationale: Surface soil wetness (top layer), not root-zone wetness; the farmers' account is a premise the reason must not confirm.

cases.question: Auckland's strongest winds across the noughties.

expected.rationale: The noughties are 2000 to 2009; the strongest-wind variable.

cases.question: Busan's winds — any change over the whole record?

cases.question: I teach a mixed class of fourteen-year-olds in a mountain town, and next term we are spending six weeks on high places and cold places. Last year the unit was mostly reading and a few videos, and the students said it felt like someone else's story. This year I want them to work with a real record and to argue carefully about what it shows. Some of them have relatives who herd yaks, and they hear many stories about the snow arriving later or leaving earlier, or about roads that used to close for weeks. I do not want to tell them those stories are right or wrong; I want them to look at a long record, see what it says and what it cannot say, and write down their doubts. I know that a model grid cell is large and that one cell over high mountains will not match one valley. I also know that a single line through noisy years can mislead, so I would like them to see the yearly values first and only then talk about rates. We will spend one lesson on what a reanalysis is, one on units, and one on why a short record is weak evidence. The students will work in pairs and present a short summary at the end. Please keep it simple enough for them, and do not suggest anything that needs a paid account or special software. So, concretely: please set up snow depth on the Tibetan Plateau from 1990 to 2020.

expected.rationale: A long but valid question ending in a fully specified request.

cases.question: Sea ice near Anchorage from 1985 to 2015. Some context, in case it matters: I am a retired harbour pilot and I am writing a short memoir chapter about the winters I worked on Cook Inlet. My notes from those years are patchy. Some winters I wrote down the dates the ice first troubled the shipping lanes, other winters I wrote nothing at all, and a few notebooks were lost in a move. My grandson says there is a free NASA record that might help me check my memory against something more systematic. I understand it will be a large grid cell and not the exact inlet, and that a model estimate is not the same as what I saw from the bridge. I am not looking for a forecast, and I do not need anything about the causes. I just want to see the yearly values laid out so I can compare them with my notes, and I would like to keep the period to the years I actually worked. Please do not change the dates; if the record does not cover them, tell me rather than picking other years. Thank you for your patience with an old sailor.

expected.rationale: A long but valid question opening with a fully specified request.
